Heart valve surgery costs vary considerably depending on the type of procedure, the valve involved, and what cost components are included. For aortic valve replacement, peer-reviewed research reports average inpatient costs of approximately $59,000–$64,000: one 2020 study cited an average of about $59,000 for aortic valve replacement [d2], a journal study found 6-month inpatient costs of $59,743 for surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) and $64,395 for transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) [d4], and another study reported TAVR at $60,063 versus SAVR at $60,319 [d7]. For mitral valve procedures, costs tend to be lower, with the mean cost of mitral valve repair reported at $30,720 and median at $28,717 [d5], while older data from Columbia University showed mitral valve replacement at around $14,469 per patient [d3]. A broader estimate from Statista (citing the Medical Tourism Association) placed the average total cost of heart valve replacement in the United States at $170,000 in 2021, compared to roughly $22,500 in Mexico and $20,000 in Colombia [d6]. Beyond the surgery itself, total costs also include surgeon fees, post-surgical medications, and ongoing follow-up care, all of which vary by insurance coverage and individual patient needs [d1], and complications can substantially increase annual healthcare costs [d9].
